planner.heading: Treatment Planning Tool

rings.label: Community / Structural
rings.description: The systems and conditions around the client and their family: access to care, the neighborhood, community organizations, and structural factors like poverty, discrimination and policy.

rings.label: School
rings.description: Where the client spends most of their day: academics, school climate, belonging, and the staff who know them.

rings.label: Family
rings.description: The client's home and caregivers: relationships, communication, supervision, and stress at home.

rings.label: Peer
rings.description: Friends, classmates, romantic relationships and online connections.

rings.label: Client (Individual)
rings.description: The young person at the center: their thoughts, feelings and behaviors, history, coping skills and strengths.

emailPlan.buttonLabel: Email My Plan to the Rise Team
emailPlan.hint: Opt-in — opens your email client with a plain-text summary of what you entered (factors, severities, and interventions), not the formatted PDF. Please remove or de-identify any client details before sending. Sharing this helps the Rise and toolkit development team improve the service.

planner.intro:
With only 12 sessions, this tool keeps you focused on the core goal of Rise's treatment: reducing suicidal thoughts and behaviors.

First, map the risk and protective factors in your client's world, from the individual to the community, to find the right treatment targets. Then choose evidence-based practices for each target to build your plan.

phase3Checklist.heading: Phase 3 Checklist
phase3Checklist.intro: Activities to complete before your final session with the client.

items.text: Assess and consolidate skills, and promote self-efficacy
items.detail: Review which skills have helped most, practice them once more, and help the client name what they can now do on their own.
Link the client from treatment to their next step: a warm handoff to ongoing care, school supports, or community resources.

items.text: Reflect on the Rise treatment experience and complete final screenings
items.detail: Look back on progress together, and re-administer screenings to measure change in suicidal thoughts and behaviors since intake.
Update warning signs, coping strategies, and supports so the plan reflects where the client is now.

levels.heading: Youth at the center: the five levels you'll map
levels.intro: Your client sits at the center of an ecosystem. In the planner, you map the risk and protective factors at each level, working from the outside in.
levels.hint: Click a ring or a level to see what belongs there.

tour.doLabel: What you do in the planner

phases.intention: Understand what is driving the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors, and keep them safe.

tasks.title: Map the client's ecosystem
tasks.text: Add risk and protective factors at each level, and rate how strongly each one affects the client.

tasks.title: Choose the top factors
tasks.text: Pick the factors most tied to suicidal thoughts and behaviors. These become your treatment targets.

phases.intention: Build skills that target those drivers, so the client can manage suicidal thoughts when they come up.

tasks.title: Select interventions
tasks.text: Match evidence-based practices from the Treatment Library to each top factor.

phases.intention: Make the progress last after Rise ends, and link the client to their next step in care.

tasks.title: Review and print your plan
tasks.text: See your full three-phase plan, add notes for each phase, and download a PDF.

tasks.title: Wrap up with the Phase 3 checklist
tasks.text: Re-screen, revisit the safety plan, link to care, and file an extension if needed.

orientation.note: What you enter stays in this browser. Remove or de-identify client details before you print or share.

planner.emptyStateText: Add at least one risk or protective factor above, then generate a plan.

goal.label: Goal
goal.statement: Reduce the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors

steps.ring: As you map this level, ask: what here raises or lowers the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors?
steps.topFactors: Choose the factors most closely tied to the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors. These become the focus of treatment.
steps.resourcePlan: Pick interventions that directly target what drives the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors, or strengthen what protects against them.
steps.review: Every phase of this plan works toward one outcome: reducing the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
steps.orientation: Keep one question in mind as you go: what raises or lowers this client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors?

phases.focus: Understand what is driving the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors, and keep them safe while you work on them. Assess current risk, build a safety plan together, and map the factors that raise and lower them.
phases.check: Do I know what is driving this client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors, and is a safety plan in place?

phases.focus: Give the client skills to manage suicidal thoughts when they show up and lower them over time. Teach and practice emotion regulation, problem-solving, and support-seeking, aimed at the top factors you identified.
phases.check: Is the client using these skills when suicidal thoughts or urges come up?

phases.focus: Make the reduction in suicidal thoughts and behaviors last after Rise ends. Consolidate skills, re-screen to measure change since intake, update the safety plan, and link the client to their next step in care.
phases.check: Have the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors decreased since intake, and is care in place to keep it that way?

planner.stepHint: Enter as many or as few factors as apply at this level — you can leave it blank and move on if it isn't relevant to this client.
planner.reviewIntro: Here's the full map from what you entered. Add, remove, or adjust anything before generating the plan.
planner.disclaimer: This tool offers a starting point, not a clinical decision. Always apply your own clinical judgment, and follow your standard risk assessment and safety planning protocol.

extension.phase2Text: Need more time to build and practice skills?
extension.phase3Text: If the client needs more sessions before you wrap up, file an extension with Rise.

journey.heading: Your toolkit across a Rise treatment
journey.intro: Rise treatment moves through three phases. Each one shows what to focus on, the tools that do the most work, and sample evidence-based interventions.

phases.note: Assess risk, build the safety plan together, and map what is driving the client's suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
Choose evidence-based interventions for the top factors and practice skills in session.
Re-screen, revisit the safety plan, and link the client to their next step in care.

phases.title: Phase 2: Train & Teach Skills
interventions: DBT skills: distress tolerance & emotion regulation

phases.title: Phase 3: Consolidate & Next Steps
interventions: Warm handoff to ongoing care provider
